nodes.label: Grouped Minor/Patch Dependency Updates
nodes.rationale: Every ecosystem (npm for frontend/docs/emails, pip for backend/bulk, uv for etl, github-actions) declares a `*-minor-patch` group with a per-directory open-PR cap (5 for the two largest surfaces, 3 elsewhere). Grouping collapses routine version bumps into one reviewable PR per surface instead of flooding the queue; the caps bound how much CI a weekly run can consume.

nodes.label: Backend Quality Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs basedpyright, full backend unittest discovery, and MCP live-transport tests under SKIP_MAIN_DB_REFLECTION=1 so CI never needs the private MariaDB. Exposed as `workflow_call` so Deploy Backend can reuse it as a gate; the push trigger is deliberately narrowed to only this file, because pushes to main touching backend/** already run it through the gated deploy workflow and listing backend/** here would duplicate the run.

nodes.label: basedpyright JSON Error Gate
nodes.rationale: basedpyright is run with `--outputjson ... || true`, then an inline Python script parses generalDiagnostics and exits 1 only when severity == 'error'. Swallowing the tool's own exit code and re-deciding from the JSON lets warnings pass while errors still fail the build, and caps printed diagnostics at 50 so the log stays readable.

nodes.label: Cancel-Superseded Concurrency Policy (quality runs)
nodes.rationale: Quality workflows key concurrency on `${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress: true so force-pushes and rapid commits kill stale runs rather than burning CI minutes on results nobody will read.

nodes.label: Deploy Backend Workflow
nodes.rationale: Fires on pushes to main under backend/** plus a workflow_dispatch escape hatch for redeploys and rollbacks without a source change. The deploy job `needs: quality`, so flyctl only runs behind a green Backend Quality run.

nodes.label: Queued Non-Cancelling Deploy Concurrency
nodes.rationale: Deploy workflows use a fixed concurrency group (not keyed on ref) with cancel-in-progress: false, so overlapping deploys queue instead of racing and a running flyctl deploy is never killed mid-flight.

nodes.label: Deploy DB Workflow
nodes.rationale: Deploys db/** to Fly with no quality-gate job: the directory holds maintainer-only MariaDB deployment config, not application code with tests.

nodes.label: Deploy Docs Workflow
nodes.rationale: Triggers on docs/**, branding/**, and frontend/public/openapi.yaml — the docs site embeds shared brand primitives and the published OpenAPI spec, so a change to either must republish docs even though neither lives under docs/.

nodes.label: Deploy Frontend Workflow
nodes.rationale: Mirrors Deploy Backend: quality job via workflow_call, deploy job gated on `needs: quality`, queued concurrency, flyctl deploy against frontend/fly.toml + frontend/Dockerfile.

nodes.label: Frontend Quality Workflow (reusable)
nodes.rationale: `workflow_call`-only (no direct push/PR trigger) so a single definition of npm ci + test + typecheck + lint is shared by OSS Quality for PRs and by Deploy Frontend as the deploy gate, with no duplicated run on main.

nodes.label: OSS Quality Workflow
nodes.rationale: Broad open-source hygiene gate across every public surface. frontend/** appears in the pull_request paths but is intentionally omitted from the push paths, because pushes to main touching frontend/** already run the identical checks through the gated Deploy Frontend workflow.

nodes.label: Contributor Docs Existence Check
nodes.rationale: A `test -f` sweep asserts the five root contributor docs plus a README in each of backend, frontend, docs, etl, emails, bulk, and db still exist. It is a cheap structural guard against silently deleting the onboarding surface — it checks presence only, never content.

nodes.label: Docs Yarn Install Retry Loop
nodes.rationale: `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` is wrapped in a three-attempt loop with a 5s sleep before failing, absorbing transient registry flakiness so a network blip does not red the docs build.

nodes.label: Publish DB Docs Workflow
nodes.rationale: Watches the single generated artifact bulk/schema_docs/pandects.dbml. Validates the DBML before publishing to dbdocs.io under project Pandects, so a malformed generated file fails loudly instead of overwriting the hosted schema docs.

nodes.label: Public-Safe Contribution Model
nodes.rationale: The repo is open source but several workflows depend on private infrastructure only the maintainer can reach. Rather than gate the repo, contribution is steered toward a documented public-safe local mode; contributors are told to state explicitly in the PR when a workflow needs credentials they lack, instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Maintainer-Gated Areas
nodes.rationale: Live MariaDB, Cloudflare R2 publishing, Resend delivery, Zitadel config, Fly deployment/private networking, and parts of ETL/bulk are open-source code whose operational workflows are not reproducible externally. The stated rule is to keep such changes scoped and never present private infrastructure as part of normal contributor setup.

nodes.label: Narrowest-Relevant-Checks Validation Rule
nodes.rationale: Contributors run only the checks matching what they touched — backend unittest discovery, frontend test+typecheck, docs build, or targeted basedpyright/ETL tests — rather than the whole matrix. Keeps the pre-PR loop fast and avoids contributors attempting maintainer-gated ETL commands they cannot run.

nodes.label: Env Var Sensitivity Categories
nodes.rationale: Every variable across backend, frontend, ETL, emails, bulk, and db is classified as public-safe, optional, maintainer-only, or secret. The four-tier scheme lets a contributor tell at a glance which variables they can set themselves versus which imply private infrastructure, without reading subsystem code.

nodes.label: SKIP_MAIN_DB_REFLECTION Public-Safe Switch
nodes.rationale: Setting it to 1 skips reflection of the private main MariaDB schema, which is the single toggle that turns the backend from maintainer-only into contributor-runnable. Its counterpart ENABLE_MAIN_DB_REFLECTION should stay enabled only with a genuinely valid main DB connection.

nodes.label: Pandects (M&A Agreement Research Platform)
nodes.rationale: Open-source M&A agreement research platform powering pandects.org. One repo holds the web app, Flask API, docs site, ETL pipelines, email templates, and deployment helpers across frontend/, backend/, docs/, etl/, emails/, bulk/, db/, branding/, examples/, and pg/.

nodes.label: Public-Safe Local Mode Quickstart
nodes.rationale: The default onboarding path: copy only the .env.example files you need, run the backend under SKIP_MAIN_DB_REFLECTION=1 against the default local sqlite auth DB, and use the frontend/docs dev servers. Deliberately requires no MariaDB snapshot and no real Resend, R2, Zitadel, or Fly credentials. dev-all.sh still exists but is explicitly maintainer-oriented and assumes a far richer environment.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Contribution Surface
nodes.rationale: Subsystems are ranked fully contributor-friendly (frontend, docs, root docs), contributor-friendly in public-safe local mode (backend under SKIP_MAIN_DB_REFLECTION, sqlite auth work), or partially public but operationally maintainer-gated (etl, bulk, db, pg, credential-backed integrations). The last tier is readable and patchable code whose operational commands are not runnable without maintainer coordination.

nodes.label: Maintainer-Only Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Main MariaDB data on the maintainer machine, Resend template syncing, Cloudflare R2 bulk publishing, Zitadel-backed auth and MCP identity, Fly deployment and Fly-internal networking, and Fly Postgres/WireGuard access. Documentation is required to label these explicitly rather than fold them into default onboarding steps.

nodes.label: Contributor Makefile Shortcuts
nodes.rationale: A small root Makefile exposes backend-test, dev-backend-safe, frontend-test, frontend-typecheck, dev-frontend, docs-build, and etl-typecheck so the public-safe commands have short memorable names instead of long explicit-venv invocations.

nodes.label: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Private email report instead of a public GitHub issue, handled best-effort by a single maintainer with no staffed security program. Scope is limited to what a reporter can verify from tracked repo behavior — the Flask API and auth flows, config mistakes in tracked files, credential handling, and unsafe docs/examples. Reports about unverifiable private infrastructure or guessed production configuration are out of scope.

nodes.label: Best-Effort Support Model
nodes.rationale: No SLA for triage, debugging, or feature work. Help requests must state the subsystem, the exact command, the error output, and whether the reporter is in public-safe local mode or a maintainer-only workflow — that last field is what decides whether the problem is even reproducible.

nodes.label: Backend Layered Architecture (app → routes → services → models)
nodes.rationale: app.py is composition only; routes own HTTP wiring and response shaping; services own query and side-effect orchestration; models own ORM/reflection surfaces; schemas own validation; core/* owns config, error wiring, and request hooks. The layering fixes where new code goes: endpoint logic into routes+services, schemas into schemas/, DB reflection into models/, and bootstrap-only changes into app.py.
nodes.norm_label: backend layered architecture (app → routes → services → models)

nodes.label: Typed Route Dependency Injection
nodes.rationale: _build_route_deps() in app.py constructs SectionsDeps, AgreementsDeps, ReferenceDataDeps, and AuthDeps, which routes consume instead of dynamic module lookups — registration becomes explicit and typed. AccessContextProtocol is the shared access-context contract. Typing is kept strict for helper call signatures but deliberately pragmatic for reflected SQLAlchemy handles, where strictness would only add fragile casts.

nodes.label: Auth Runtime Facade Split
nodes.rationale: backend/auth/runtime.py holds no runtime logic — it is a compatibility facade over five domain modules: session_runtime (transport, cookies, auth DB/mock store, session tokens, request identity), email_runtime (normalization, Resend delivery), oauth_runtime (provider token exchange), captcha_runtime (Turnstile), and legal_runtime (acceptance validation/persistence, sign-on event logging). Splitting by domain keeps each surface independently testable while preserving the old import path.

nodes.label: Backend Testing Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Three tests encode architectural invariants as executable rules: test_route_contracts.py pins route and operationId stability, test_auth_dependencies.py pins auth dependency wiring, and test_runtime_typing_guards.py blocks broad file-level pyright suppressions, restricts Callable[..., Any] in routes/deps.py to spots where SQLAlchemy expression typing is genuinely dynamic, and enforces that auth/runtime.py stays facade-sized with no logic definitions.

nodes.label: Public API Stability Contract
nodes.rationale: The architecture refactor is explicitly behavior-preserving: no endpoint additions or removals, no request/response schema changes, no auth/session/CORS changes. Internal contracts are stated instead as typed register_*_routes signatures returning Blueprints, so restructuring is visible internally and invisible externally.

nodes.label: Pandects MCP Server (/mcp)
nodes.rationale: A read-only authenticated MCP server exposed at /mcp with protected-resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. It is an OAuth protected resource, so browser sessions and X-API-Key auth deliberately do not work there — requests must carry Authorization: Bearer. Codex clients can fail at `codex mcp login` when the backing identity provider does not expose OAuth dynamic client registration.

nodes.label: ZITADEL OIDC Configuration for MCP
nodes.rationale: Discovery via MCP_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL is preferred over pinning MCP_OIDC_JWKS_URL directly in production, since a pinned JWKS breaks on key rotation. MCP_OIDC_AUDIENCE must match the audience ZITADEL actually stamps into the MCP access token; issuer and authorization-server URL are normally identical for ZITADEL.

nodes.label: MCP Four-Scope Authorization Model
nodes.rationale: Every tool declares its required scopes in backend/mcp/tools/__init__.py against four scopes: agreements:search (discovery/listing), agreements:read (single-agreement metadata), sections:search (all section, snippet, taxonomy, and reference-data tools), and agreements:read_fulltext. The last is a redaction switch rather than an access switch — without it, agreement XML is still returned but stays redacted.

nodes.label: Self-Describing Tool Surface (no hand-maintained inventory)
nodes.rationale: MCP.md refuses to list the 23 shipped tools because a hand-maintained inventory in this file once drifted 20 tools behind the server before anyone noticed. The authoritative list is whatever tools/list returns; get_server_capabilities serves the same inventory with per-tool selection hints and negative guidance, and the maintained prose lives in docs/docs/mcp/technical-details.md.

nodes.label: Website Auth Cutover to ZITADEL-Backed Pandects Pages
nodes.rationale: Pandects owns /login, /signup, /reset-password, and /reset-password/confirm, backed by the same ZITADEL identity that authenticates MCP. First sign-in validates the token server-side, reuses the local user if issuer+subject is already in auth_external_subjects, otherwise auto-links by verified email or creates and links a new local user, then forces a legal-acceptance step before issuing the local session. The cutover removed the separate MCP-specific connect flow from the website UI.
nodes.norm_label: website auth cutover to zitadel-backed pandects pages

nodes.label: ZITADEL-Owned Auth Email Delivery
nodes.rationale: Pandects exposes a signed notification endpoint (POST /v1/auth/zitadel/notifications/email, verified via the Zitadel-Signature header and a provider signing key), but verification and password-reset email delivery are deliberately left ZITADEL-owned to avoid duplicate sends to the same user.

nodes.label: Legacy Manual External-Subject Linking API
nodes.rationale: The low-level GET/POST/DELETE /v1/auth/external-subjects endpoints survive the auto-linking cutover, retained for migration and admin use rather than as part of any normal sign-in path.

nodes.label: Alembic-Managed Auth DB Schema
nodes.rationale: Only the auth DB is migrated (backend/alembic.ini, backend/migrations/); the main MariaDB is reflected and never migrated from here. backend.init_auth_db applies migrations and bootstraps a fresh database, and runs automatically as the Fly release command in production. App startup runs create_all only for the implicit local dev/test sqlite — a configured database is never altered at startup, so schema changes cannot sneak in through a deploy.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Generation Command
nodes.rationale: `python -m backend.app openapi` regenerates the spec from the live Flask app under SKIP_MAIN_DB_REFLECTION=1, so the checked-in OpenAPI file is derived from the route/schema code rather than hand-edited.

nodes.label: Pandects v1 REST API Surface
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI 3.0.2 spec served from https://api.pandects.org (local dev at http://localhost:5113). Groups paths under tags for sections, agreements, tax-clauses, agreements_search, taxonomy, tax-clause-taxonomy, naics, counsel, and dumps, with named operationIds (listSections, searchAgreements, getAgreement, getTaxonomy, listDumps, …) that the route-contract test pins.

nodes.label: PaginationMetadata Response Envelope
nodes.rationale: A shared component carrying total, total_pages, first_page, last_page, page, previous_page, and next_page, reused across every list endpoint so clients get one pagination shape instead of per-resource variants.

nodes.label: Backend Python Dependency Stack
nodes.rationale: Fully pinned. Flask 3.1.3 with flask-smorest + apispec + marshmallow + webargs for the schema-driven OpenAPI surface, SQLAlchemy 2.0 with mysqlclient/PyMySQL for the main DB and psycopg2-binary for the auth Postgres, alembic for auth migrations, PyJWT + cryptography for MCP/OIDC token verification, boto3 for R2, defusedxml for untrusted agreement XML, gunicorn for serving, and basedpyright pinned as a runtime-installed dev tool so CI and local type checks use the same version.

nodes.label: Shared Brand Primitives
nodes.rationale: branding/ centralizes links.json (canonical public URLs for app-to-app navigation), tokens.css (shared high-level color tokens), and logo assets so the app, docs, and related surfaces cannot drift. It is explicitly shared infrastructure: changing user-visible links or assets obliges updating docs and screenshots too.

nodes.label: NER Package Current State
nodes.rationale: Deliberately describes only the supported present-day state (ARTICLE/SECTION/PAGE structural tagging, boundary_mix sampling, raw metrics, parquet input) rather than historical experiments, so readers do not resurrect removed paths.

nodes.label: Deprecated NER Artifacts Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Regex/snap code, legacy sampling, and the dead postprocessing harness were removed and old artifacts relocated under etl/src/etl/models/deprecated/ to keep exactly one supported modeling path.

nodes.label: boundary_mix Sampling
nodes.rationale: Only sampling mode kept after legacy sampling was removed; concentrates training windows on structural boundaries where ARTICLE/SECTION/PAGE decisions are hard.

nodes.label: split_version Manifest Keying
nodes.rationale: Splits are assigned by agreement_uuid (not page_uuid) and frozen per split_version so tuning, grid sweeps, and final training compare against identical holdouts; agreements with only article_upsample rows stay train-only to avoid contaminating eval.

nodes.label: ner.py tune (Optuna HPO)
nodes.rationale: Runs on train/val only so the test split stays untouched until final-train.

nodes.label: ner.py final-train (Test-Set Evaluation)
nodes.rationale: The test split is evaluated exactly once, for the recipe selected on validation; winning architectural and window flags must be passed explicitly so the final run reproduces the selected XP recipe.

nodes.label: audit-articles Failure Export
nodes.rationale: Inspection-only path over an existing checkpoint (no retraining) so strict-boundary ARTICLE failures can be reviewed right after a validation run.

nodes.label: Frozen Grid Training Recipe
nodes.rationale: Hyperparameters are frozen (lr 5e-5, wd 0.01, warmup 10%) so grid rows isolate architectural variables instead of confounding them with optimizer differences.

nodes.label: 512/510/256 Window-Stride Setting
nodes.rationale: train_subsample_window 512 with val_window 510 and val_stride 256 gives overlapping validation windows so boundary tokens are never evaluated only at a window edge.

nodes.label: Category Match Test (Operative-Function Rule)
nodes.rationale: Assignment must turn on whether the candidate's core legal concept IS the section's operative function, not on topical overlap or shared vocabulary — this stops the classifier from labelling by keyword co-occurrence.

nodes.label: Empty-List Abstention Over Nearest Neighbor
nodes.rationale: Returning [] is preferred to down-grading to a related-but-distinct neighbor (e.g., a hedging/transfer restriction is not an ordinary-course-conduct covenant), because a wrong specific label is more damaging downstream than a null.

nodes.label: 'Other / Unclassified' Is Not a Fallback
nodes.rationale: Reserved for sections that are substantively residual/miscellaneous; used as a catch-all it would silently absorb true misses and make the residual bucket uninterpretable.

nodes.label: Do Not Abstain On Short or Statute-Naming Reps
nodes.rationale: Brevity is not ambiguity: a one-line 'not an investment company' rep is still a compliance-with-laws representation, so length or statute references must not trigger abstention.
nodes.norm_label: do not abstain on short or statute-naming reps

nodes.label: Representation Side Resolution (Authoritative)
nodes.rationale: The representing party is fixed by article_title, never by prose, because rep text routinely discusses the counterparty and would otherwise flip the side label.

nodes.label: article_title Overrides Section-Text Inference
nodes.rationale: Two-step resolution: generic side naming first, then entity-to-side mapping via transaction context (Merger Sub/Holdco/acquisition vehicles = Buyer side; target, subsidiaries, selling principals = Company side).

nodes.label: Reciprocal Non-Reliance Disclaimer Exception
nodes.rationale: Disclaimer / 'no other representations' clauses are written reciprocally, so their prose describes both parties; the side still comes from the containing article.

nodes.label: DeepSeek Taxonomy Enrichment Index (202 nodes)
nodes.rationale: Each node carries standard_id, level (l2/l3), description, canonical_terms, example_phrases, and exclusion_cues so retrieval candidates arrive with both positive and negative signal instead of a bare label.

nodes.label: Exclusion Cues (Negative Boundary Signal)
nodes.rationale: Every leaf states where it does NOT apply (e.g., bring-down conditions vs. the reps themselves vs. indemnity survival) so near-neighbor leaves are separated at candidate-selection time.

nodes.label: L2 Umbrella Nodes Route To Child Leaves
nodes.rationale: L2 groupings (e.g., Buyer/Parent Conditions) are explicitly marked as non-operative umbrellas whose example_phrases instruct the model to prefer a specific sub-leaf whenever one concept dominates.
